subject.title: fix(cron): treat isolated setup phases as progress

question: After the unused-stage blocker is fixed, should this external PR require redacted live scheduled-cron proof, or should maintainers explicitly override the proof gate with focused regression proof?
rationale: ClawSweeper policy treats tests and fake timers as supplemental for external PRs, while this change affects availability-sensitive cron timeout behavior that maintainers may decide to waive with an explicit override.

options.title: Require live cron proof
options.body: Ask for redacted scheduled-cron terminal output, copied live output, or runtime logs showing setup progress surviving past the old 60-second cutoff before merge.

options.title: Override with regression proof
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the fake-timer regression proof as sufficient after the unused-stage blocker is fixed.

options.title: Pick a sibling contract
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer a narrower before_agent_reply phase-emission fix from a sibling PR.

recommendation.title: Require live cron proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted scheduled-cron terminal output, copied live output, or runtime logs showing setup progress surviving past the old 60-second cutoff before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current watchdog module boundary dates to steipete's cron timer split, and the remaining choice is proof sufficiency for that runtime behavior.
